hints: Look at the overall pattern first. Notice the ring of separate dark bundles around a large central tissue. What stem structure does this tell you it is?
Remember the order inside one stem vascular bundle from outside to inside is phloem, then cambium, then xylem with its big open vessels.
walkthrough:
**Identify the organ from the pattern**

This is a transverse section of a young dicot stem. You can tell because there is a ring of separate vascular bundles surrounding a central pith, not a central star or scattered bundles.

**Recall what is inside a stem bundle**

In each bundle, the phloem is toward the outside of the stem and the xylem is toward the inside (centre) of the stem. Xylem vessels stand out as a few large, round, empty-looking, thick-walled tubes.

**Match the labels to the tissues**

Label B points right into the middle of a vascular bundle on the inner side, where those large open xylem vessels are. Label A is outer, label C is central pith, and label D is the outer part of a bundle. So B is the xylem vessels.

options.A: This points to the outer side of the vascular bundle, which is phloem and associated fibres, not the large inner xylem vessels.
options.B: This points to the large, wide-lumen vessels on the inner side of the vascular bundle, which is exactly where xylem vessels are found in a stem.
options.C: This points to the large, thin-walled parenchyma cells in the centre, which is the pith for storage, not conducting xylem.
options.D: This points to the outer region of a bundle, the phloem side, so it cannot be the inner xylem vessels.
